chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a servant says 'Allah knows' but he is lying, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Did you not find anyone else to lie upon besides Me?!'

key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God (Allah 'azza wa jalla)
key_terms.علم الله: The formula 'Allah knows' used as an oath or attestation
key_terms.كاذبا: Lying, being untruthful — refers to the servant's false invocation

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about swearing falsely in the name of Allah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports a severe divine reprimand for those who invoke Allah's name in a false oath. The hadith presents God's reproach as a rhetorical question — 'Did you not find anyone else to lie about except Me?' — conveying that such a person has singled out God as the one in whose name they falsely swear, making their transgression all the more contemptible. This reflects the serious gravity of using 'Allah knows' (علم الله) as a false attestation, which was a common formula in classical Arabic culture to assert the truth of something.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
